method: Mann-Kendall (Hamed-Rao autocorrelation correction) + Sen slope on deseasonalized monthly GRACE/GRACE-FO TWS (GFZ GravIS, 1-degree), 2002-04..2026-08; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR q<0.05 across basins. Basin value = cos(latitude)-weighted mean of grid cells whose centres lie in the basin (nearest land cell if none). Deseasonalized by subtracting each calendar month's mean; missing months (incl. the 2017-18 mission gap) are not interpolated; Sen slope is computed on the real time axis. Precipitation: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) PRECTOTCORR monthly at up to 3 points per basin, same test on deseasonalized anomalies, slope as % of mean per decade, separate BH-FDR.

definitions.trend_class: drying / wetting if TWS BH-FDR q < 0.05 with negative / positive Sen slope, else no_significant_trend
definitions.low_resolution: no GRACE cell centre inside the basin (nearest cell used) or basin area < 50,000 km2; GRACE effective resolution is ~300 km, so the value mostly reflects the surrounding region
definitions.possible_groundwater_signal: TWS drying but precipitation shows no significant decline (precip q >= 0.05 or slope >= 0); the storage loss may come from groundwater pumping, not rainfall
definitions.series.tws_anom_cm: deseasonalized TWS anomaly (what the trend test uses); series.tws_cm keeps the seasonal cycle (GravIS anomaly vs. its own reference); trend line = sen_intercept_cm + sen_slope_cm_per_month * months since 2002-04
definitions.name: derived label: largest GPPD hydro plant in the basin + main countries (>= 10% of basin GW)

summary.headline: 392 GW of hydropower (37% of the 1053 GW mapped) sits in 221 basins with a significant drying trend in GRACE water storage since 2002; 343 GW sits in 108 significantly wetting basins.

limitations: GRACE TWS is the sum of all water: groundwater, soil moisture, snow, lakes and reservoirs. Declines in heavily irrigated regions (e.g. north India, the North China Plain, the Middle East) can come from groundwater pumping and need not mean less river flow for hydropower; such basins are flagged possible_groundwater_signal.
Reservoir filling itself raises TWS (e.g. new dams in China, Ethiopia), which can mask or create trends.
GRACE's effective resolution is ~300 km; level-4 basins smaller than that, or with no 1-degree cell centre inside, carry the regional signal (low_resolution).
Trends over 2002-2026 (about 24 years) are sensitive to the start and end years and to multi-year climate variability (e.g. ENSO); a significant trend is not proof of a permanent change.
The 2017-07..2018-05 GRACE/GRACE-FO gap and other missing months are left missing; the inter-mission bias is handled by GFZ's processing, not by us.

Precipitation is MERRA-2 reanalysis (NASA POWER) at a few points per basin, standing in for GPM IMERG (which needs an Earthdata login); it is less accurate than gauge-corrected products in data-sparse regions.
Basins are weighted by installed capacity in WRI GPPD v1.3 (2021); plants built since then are missing.
Glacier and ice-sheet mass loss (e.g. Alaska, Patagonia, High Mountain Asia) appears as TWS decline and may leak into neighbouring basins at GRACE resolution.
notes: GravIS has two solutions dated in the same calendar month for 2011-10, 2015-04; they are averaged.
35 of 293 months have no GRACE/GRACE-FO solution (including the 2017-07..2018-05 mission gap); they are left missing, not interpolated.
Precipitation trend unavailable for 1 basins (POWER request failed, data incomplete, or mean rainfall < 0.05 mm/day); their precip fields are null.
